doc.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Her 1965 album and recordings she now finds ridiculous
summary: Brown names 'Ruth Brown '65' on Mainstream, reissued as 'Softly', and compares it to early hits like 'Lucky Lips'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Tell us one of the ones that’s pretty good. Tell us one of the ones that you think is classic.
I did an album in 1965 called “Ruth Brown ‘65” on Mainstream. The company went out of business. The record has been re-issued this year on SONY under a new name, it’s

now called “Softly.” And in that album I did “Here’s That Rainy Day,” I did “Why Do You Whisper Green Grass” which was an old Bill Kenny tune from the Inkspots, you know which dates back to my youth. And in that I also did “Porgy” — “I Love You Porgy.” Things that I had forgotten that I’d ever touched on. And I was listening to that album and I said, [whistles] I didn’t sound bad, you know? And then you go back and get some things like “Lucky Lips” and “This Little Girl’s Gone Rockin’” and “I Wrote My Momma a Letter When I Had Long Silky Curls” and right now it sounds kind of ridiculous. They say, “Would you sing that song?” Are you kidding? I don’t know what made me sing it then, you know? But it does make a difference.
